rows.why_long: PrizePicks higher 1.5 needs 57% per pick for your entry; fair view 74% (fanduel 2.5, moved to this line). Averaging 1.6 over the last 8 games, higher than 1.5 in 36% of them (raw 52%, shrunk 71%). Projects 2.0 (raw 63%, shrunk 72%).
why_points: The pick: Receptions higher 1.5 on PrizePicks. Each pick has to win 57% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 2.5, moved to this line) is 74%.
Game log, most recent first: 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1, 3. Weighted average 1.6; went higher than 1.5 in 3 of 8 games (36% recency-weighted).
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±0.9, so the line is 0.2 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — basically a coin flip.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): -9% on his average.
PFF: CIN plays man on 33% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 30%); he gains 1.15 yds/route vs man and 1.31 vs zone → -0% from scheme.
PFF: CIN allows 1.43 yds/route to WRs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.57) → -11% against his usual opponents.

PFF: He runs 17% of his routes from the slot (1.45 yds/route there, 1.14 outside); CIN allows 1.60 yds/route to slot WRs and 1.36 outside (league 1.52 / 1.60, opponent-adjusted) → -12% vs his usual opponents.
PFF: 39% of his targets are intermediate (10-19 yds) (league 23%); CIN allows 9.8 yds/target there (league 9.7) → -2% from depth.
Projection: we expect 2.0 catches on average — 0.5 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 52% and the matchup 63%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 71%, matchup 72%.
Bottom line: we give it 72% to win and it needs 57%. The edge is the difference: +14.7 points; that works out to about +26¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: low line - one play can decide it.
